# Privacy, Security & Delivery Checklist: Devices & Push Notifications

**Purpose**: Unit tests for the requirements of spec 023 — push token handling, payload privacy, removal, retries, dedupe, quiet hours and the frozen API contract
**Created**: 2026-10-06
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

Depth: standard release gate. Audience: PR reviewer. Defaults applied (owner away): focus on token/payload privacy and delivery reliability.

## Token handling — Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are all places the push token must never appear enumerated (response, logs at every level, exceptions, job payloads, events, audit, operator screens)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK002 Is the at-rest protection of the token specified with the same properties the baseline requires (authenticated, per-record nonce, key id beside the value)? [Consistency, Spec §FR-006, Baseline rule 4]
- [ ] CHK003 Is key rotation for the token keyring specified (how a new key becomes active and how values sealed under an old key remain readable)? [Gap, Spec §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK004 Is the moment the token is decrypted bounded (only by the delivery, immediately before sending)? [Clarity, Spec Clarifications]
- [ ] CHK005 Is the accepted token format quantified (length, character set) so validation is testable? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002]
- [ ] CHK006 Are the service-account key, the signed assertion and the OAuth access token covered by the never-log rule, not only the push token? [Gap, Plan R-16]

## Registration lifecycle — Scenario Coverage

- [ ] CHK007 Is every session end reason mapped to registration removal, including idle expiry and the purge's `account_deleted`? [Coverage, Spec §FR-009, US1·6]
- [ ] CHK008 Is the window between a session ending and the queued removal closed by a stated requirement? [Coverage, Spec §FR-011]
- [ ] CHK009 Is the behaviour defined when one token arrives under a second session (same phone, other account)? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-004]
- [ ] CHK010 Is the answer for another person's, another own, ended or unknown session id specified identically, so existence is not disclosed? [Consistency, Spec §FR-001, §6]
- [ ] CHK011 Is idle expiry quantified and justified? [Clarity, Spec §FR-010]

## Payload privacy — Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK012 Is the forbidden content list explicit (amount, balance, currency, names of wallet/category/person, note, address, date of money, token, URL)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-020]
- [ ] CHK013 Is the allowed key set for every message type listed, with nothing left open-ended? [Completeness, Spec §5 table]
- [ ] CHK014 Do the visible title and body carry the same restrictions as the data block (no placeholders, names, amounts, dates)? [Consistency, Spec §FR-021]
- [ ] CHK015 Is the language of the text defined, including when the language changes while a message is held? [Clarity, Spec §FR-021, Clarifications]
- [ ] CHK016 Is the summary message free of a count or any volume signal? [Clarity, Plan A-5]
- [ ] CHK017 Is the `role` value in `member_role_changed` justified as non-sensitive and limited to an enum? [Clarity, Spec §FR-020]

## Delivery reliability — Exception & Recovery Flows

- [ ] CHK018 Are retryable and permanent provider failures enumerated, each with its outcome? [Completeness, Spec §FR-033, §FR-034, Plan R-9]
- [ ] CHK019 Is a provider "invalid argument" not caused by the token distinguished from an invalid token, so a good registration is not pruned? [Edge Case, Plan A-11]
- [ ] CHK020 Is the retry budget quantified (attempts, backoff, Retry-After) and its terminal state defined? [Clarity, Spec §FR-033, §FR-035]
- [ ] CHK021 Is recovery from a worker crash mid-delivery specified without double sending? [Recovery, Spec §FR-036, §FR-049]
- [ ] CHK022 Is the behaviour of a scheduled pass when one source query or one recipient fails specified (isolation, no aborted pass)? [Gap, Exception Flow]
- [ ] CHK023 Is expired-access-token handling specified (refresh once, then retry)? [Coverage, Spec Edge Cases]

## Dedupe and "already notified" — Consistency

- [ ] CHK024 Is a dedupe key defined for every source, and do the spec, data model and research agree on them? [Consistency, Spec §3, Data model]
- [ ] CHK025 Is the "once per budget per period" rule stated with the exact crossing condition (strictly above) and period definition? [Clarity, Spec §FR-026, US4·6]
- [ ] CHK026 Are past-period edits, archived budgets and limit decreases each covered? [Coverage, Spec US4, Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK027 Is the backlog behaviour for occurrences after an outage or at rollout bounded? [Coverage, Spec §FR-023, US3·7]
- [ ] CHK028 Is it stated that turning a category back on never resends what was skipped? [Clarity, Spec Edge Cases]

## Quiet hours and limits — Measurability

- [ ] CHK029 Are quiet-hour bounds, granularity and the start = end case specified? [Clarity, Spec §FR-016]
- [ ] CHK030 Is the release behaviour defined when the person turns quiet hours off or moves them while messages are held? [Gap, Spec §FR-017]
- [ ] CHK031 Is the interaction between a burst of released held messages and the rate limit specified? [Gap, Edge Case]
- [ ] CHK032 Are DST transitions addressed for quiet hours and the reminder hour? [Coverage, Spec Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK033 Are the rate limits quantified per person per hour and per day, and the over-limit outcome defined (dropped, not delayed)? [Measurability, Spec §FR-028]

## API contract completeness

- [ ] CHK034 Does every operation list every status it can return, matching the shared refusals of the runtime? [Completeness, Spec §5, notifications.yaml]
- [ ] CHK035 Are request and response examples present for every operation and for the payload? [Completeness, notifications.yaml]
- [ ] CHK036 Are the preference keys, quiet-hours behaviour and payload schema — C16's three needs — each frozen in one place? [Traceability, Spec §5, contracts/push-api.md]
- [ ] CHK037 Is client behaviour on unknown `type` values and on deep links to unsynced records specified? [Coverage, contracts/push-api.md]
- [ ] CHK038 Is the version bump and "no new error code" decision recorded? [Traceability, Spec §5]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK039 Is the no-new-dependency constraint stated as a requirement with the replacement path for the SDK? [Traceability, Spec §FR-040]
- [ ] CHK040 Are production-safety rules for non-delivering gateways specified (log refused, fcm without credentials refused, disabled allowed and honest)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-041, §FR-042]
- [ ] CHK041 Are the owner decisions still open listed with whether each blocks? [Traceability, Spec §9]
- [ ] CHK042 Is the assumption that every session end publishes `DeviceSessionEnded` validated against spec 007/022? [Assumption, Spec Assumptions]

## Notes

- Agent evaluation (owner away, delegated): every item was read against the spec and plan. Gaps found and fixed in the spec in the same run: CHK003 (key rotation → FR-006), CHK006 (secrets never logged → FR-007), CHK022 (pass isolation → FR-051), CHK030 (release on preference change → FR-017), CHK031 (released burst vs rate limit → Edge Cases). CHK042 was validated in code: `EndSessions::end` dispatches `DeviceSessionEnded` for every reason, and `PurgeAccount::begin` ends sessions through it. The markers stay unchecked: they belong to the reviewer.
- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
